paragraphs: It is different for the common people. Ordinary working people have little time for school. Their parents often cannot pay for their food, even when they are very young. When the children are old enough to work, they must start a job. They need this job to earn money for food and a home. This work is usually very simple, and it is the same every day. So it does not make them use their minds very much. Also, they work all the time, and the work is very hard. So they have little free time. They also do not want to learn other things, or even think about them.

In a modern country, common people cannot learn as much as rich people or people from important families. But the most important parts of education are reading, writing and counting. Children can learn these things when they are very young. Most of them have time to learn them before they start work. This is true even for children who will later do the lowest jobs. The state can help with this, and it does not need much money. It can make learning easier for almost all people. It can encourage them. It can even make it a rule for everyone.

How can the state make it easier? It can open a little school in every parish or district. A parish is a small area around a church. In this school, children learn for a very small price, so even a poor worker can pay. The state pays part of the teacher's money, but not all of it. Why not all? Because if the state paid all or most of it, the teacher would soon stop doing his work well. In Scotland, these parish schools have taught almost all the common people to read. Many of them have also learned to write and count. In England, charity schools have done the same thing. But there are fewer of these schools, so fewer people have learned. In these little schools, the reading books could teach more. Sometimes the children of poor people learn a little Latin there. But this Latin almost never helps them. It would be better to teach them the first parts of geometry and mechanics. Geometry is the study of shapes and lines. Mechanics is the study of machines and movement. Then the education of these people would perhaps be as good as possible. Almost every common job gives people chances to use geometry and mechanics. So, little by little, workers would get better at these ideas. These ideas are the first step to the greatest and the most useful sciences.
The state can also encourage children to learn. It can give small prizes and little badges to the children of common people who are very good at these things.

Last, the state can make learning necessary for almost everyone. How? Every man must take a test in reading, writing and counting. He must pass it before he can join a trade group in a town. A trade group is a group of people who do the same work. Without the test, he cannot start his own business in a village or a town.
